column1: # Claude Code cloud-session profiles — what a session of each kind gets.
# WHY: a cloud session starts as a bare Ubuntu sandbox with none of this repo's CLI
# tooling and none of its credentials. //tools/cloud-bootstrap reads THIS file, keyed on
# the $VITRUVIAN_PROFILE environment variable set on the cloud environment, to decide
# two things: which CLIs to install, and which identity + secrets the session may hold.
# The profile is the BLAST-RADIUS BOUNDARY. Each row names one service account and the
# exact secret list that account may materialise; a session running `core` cannot reach
# a Pulumi token or a cluster credential even if one exists, because its row does not
# list them and its SA has no IAM to read them. Add capability by adding a row, never by
# widening an existing one.
# WANT ONE KEY THAT UNLOCKS EVERYTHING? That is the `all` row, and it is the default.
# One service account, one $VITRUVIAN_CLOUD_KEY, every credential the agent needs. The
# narrower rows exist for when you deliberately want a session that CANNOT reach
# production -- reviewing third-party code, or anything that ingests untrusted input --
# not because the everyday case is supposed to be complicated.
# SEVERAL PROFILES MAY ALSO BE COMBINED (VITRUVIAN_PROFILE=core,homelab), but prefer a
# single row that lists what you need: combining is the escape hatch for holding two
# EXISTING boundaries at once without defining a third, and it costs three rules that a
# single row does not. It does NOT merge privileges into one identity -- each profile
# keeps its own service account and reads only its own secrets -- so each needs its own
# key in $VITRUVIAN_CLOUD_KEY_<PROFILE> (the shared $VITRUVIAN_CLOUD_KEY can satisfy only
# one, and identity pinning refuses the rest rather than using the wrong account); the
# FIRST listed profile with an identity becomes the session's ambient GCP identity -- what
# pulumi, gsutil and a bare gcloud use; and two rows mapping the SAME env var to DIFFERENT
# secrets is refused, since which credential the session holds must not depend on row
# order. None of that applies when you use one row.
# NO SECRET VALUES LIVE HERE. This file names secrets; the values are in the declared
# project's Secret Manager (seed with //tools/gcp-secrets). The only credential on the
# cloud environment itself is $VITRUVIAN_CLOUD_KEY — the profile's SA key, which can do
# nothing but read that profile's secrets.
# FORMAT: columns separated by any whitespace (awk default), aligned with spaces for
# readability (the .tsv extension is nominal — same convention as
# infrastructure/gcp-identities.tsv). Consumers MUST skip `#` comment and blank lines.
# Columns:
#   profile     value of $VITRUVIAN_PROFILE that selects this row (the resolver key)
#   tools       comma-separated CLI keys to install; '-' for none. Known keys:
#               bazel,direnv,gh,gcloud,pulumi,kubectl,tailscale  (gcloud is added
#               automatically whenever sa_account is set, since reading the secrets
#               needs it). Combined profiles install the UNION.
#   sa_account  service account this profile authenticates as. The bootstrap REFUSES to
#               proceed if $VITRUVIAN_CLOUD_KEY belongs to a different account, so a
#               mis-pasted key cannot silently escalate a session. '-' = no GCP identity.
#   sa_project  GCP project holding this profile's secrets (also CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT);
#               '-' if the profile has no secrets
#   secrets     comma-separated ENV_VAR=secret-name pairs to materialise into the
#               session; '-' for none. An ENV_VAR already set on the environment WINS
#               and is left untouched (that is the no-GCP fallback path).
#               ENV_VAR=- means ENVIRONMENT-ONLY: the profile is entitled to it, but
#               its value is not in Secret Manager and never will be, so no read is
#               attempted. Use it for credentials another system owns -- e.g.
#               BUILDBUDDY_API_KEY, a GitHub Actions/Dependabot secret managed by
#               //infrastructure/pulumi/platform/repo_config and injected from the
#               pipeline. Declaring it keeps it inside the blast-radius boundary
#               (a profile that omits it still gets it scrubbed) without inventing a
#               Secret Manager address that would fail the day SM is wired up.
#   purpose     free text; may contain spaces; MUST be the last column

# profile  tools                          sa_account                                                              sa_project                     secrets                                                                                                        purpose

all        bazel,direnv,gh,gcloud,pulumi,kubectl,tailscale  claude-cloud-all@prj-c-bu2-infra-pipeline-3d09.iam.gserviceaccount.com    prj-c-bu2-infra-pipeline-3d09  GH_TOKEN=claude-cloud-core-github-token,BUILDBUDDY_API_KEY=-,PULUMI_ACCESS_TOKEN=claude-cloud-pulumi-token,TS_AUTHKEY=claude-cloud-ts-authkey,LAB_SA_TOKEN=claude-cloud-lab-sa-token,CLAUDE_SSH_KEY=claude-cloud-ssh-key  DEFAULT. Everything, one service account, one key. Use this unless you specifically want a narrower session.

core       bazel,direnv,gh                claude-cloud-core@prj-c-bu2-infra-pipeline-3d09.iam.gserviceaccount.com  prj-c-bu2-infra-pipeline-3d09  GH_TOKEN=claude-cloud-core-github-token,BUILDBUDDY_API_KEY=-                                   Default. Build, test, review and open PRs in the monorepo. No infrastructure credentials.

infra      bazel,direnv,gh,gcloud,pulumi  claude-cloud-infra@prj-c-bu2-infra-pipeline-3d09.iam.gserviceaccount.com  prj-c-bu2-infra-pipeline-3d09  GH_TOKEN=claude-cloud-core-github-token,BUILDBUDDY_API_KEY=-,PULUMI_ACCESS_TOKEN=claude-cloud-pulumi-token  core + Pulumi/GCP infrastructure work (preview/up against the foundation and app stacks).

homelab    bazel,direnv,gh,kubectl,tailscale        claude-cloud-lab@prj-c-bu2-infra-pipeline-3d09.iam.gserviceaccount.com   prj-c-bu2-infra-pipeline-3d09  GH_TOKEN=claude-cloud-core-github-token,TS_AUTHKEY=claude-cloud-ts-authkey,LAB_SA_TOKEN=claude-cloud-lab-sa-token,CLAUDE_SSH_KEY=claude-cloud-ssh-key  core + tailnet transport, k3s cluster admin and node SSH (feeds tailscale-up.sh / kube-setup.sh).

readonly   bazel,direnv                   -                                                                        -                              -                                                                                                              Tooling only, zero credentials. Use for untrusted input, reviews of third-party code, or a spike.
